categories.main_business_segments: FactSet operates through three primary geographic segments: Americas, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), and Asia Pacific. Within each segment, the company offers solutions tailored to four firm types: Institutional Buyside, Dealmakers, Wealth, and Partnerships & CUSIP Global Services (CGS). These segments reflect both the geographic origin of sales and the specialized needs of different financial industry client groups.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FactSet’s core technologies include an open, flexible digital platform that integrates expansive financial data, sophisticated analytics, and AI-powered tools. The company leverages a hybrid infrastructure with both proprietary data centers and leading cloud providers, and delivers solutions via configurable desktop/mobile platforms, APIs, data feeds, and cloud-based digital products. AI and automation are embedded across offerings to enhance data discovery, workflow automation, and client insights.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FactSet primarily serves institutional asset managers, wealth managers, asset owners, hedge funds, bankers, corporate users, private equity and venture capital professionals, and partners in the financial services ecosystem. Its solutions are used by research analysts, portfolio managers, traders, performance analysts, risk managers, investor relations officers, and technologists, supporting workflows across the investment lifecycle.
categories.geographic_coverage: FactSet has a global presence, with 35 offices in 19 countries and operations spanning the Americas (primarily the U.S., Canada, and Brazil), EMEA (notably the UK, Germany, France, and UAE), and Asia Pacific (including India, the Philippines, China, Japan, Singapore, and Australia). In fiscal 2025, the Americas accounted for 65% of revenue, EMEA 25%, and Asia Pacific 10%.
categories.supply_chain_position: FactSet operates as a downstream provider in the financial information supply chain, aggregating, normalizing, and delivering data, analytics, and workflow solutions directly to end users in the investment and financial services industries. The company sources data from third-party suppliers and exchanges, integrates and enhances it, and provides value-added services to clients.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: FactSet’s strategic priorities center on expanding its data ecosystem and delivery capabilities, embedding deeper into client workflows, and innovating with AI. The company invests heavily in AI and automation, cloud delivery, and workflow integration, aiming to provide comprehensive, enterprise-wide solutions and to differentiate through next-generation automation and analytics. R&D focuses on enhancing product speed, robustness, and usability, with a strong emphasis on AI-driven innovation.
categories.revenue_model: FactSet generates the majority of its revenue from recurring subscriptions to its multi-asset class data, analytics, and technology solutions, delivered via its connected platform. Additional revenue streams include managed services, professional services, and licensing of proprietary identifiers (e.g., CUSIP/CGS). Annual Subscription Value (ASV) is a key metric, reflecting forward-looking recurring revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FactSet operates in a highly competitive market, with major competitors including Bloomberg L.P., S&P Global’s Market Intelligence division, and London Stock Exchange Group’s Data & Analytics division (formerly Refinitiv). Other notable competitors are BlackRock Aladdin, MSCI, and Morningstar. FactSet positions itself as a comprehensive, open, and flexible platform with deep workflow integration and strong client service.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, FactSet reported revenues of $2.32 billion (up 5.4% year-over-year), net income of $597 million (up 11.2%), and an operating margin of 32.2%. Organic ASV grew 5.7% to $2.37 billion, with over 8,996 clients and 237,324 users. The company maintains high retention rates (over 95% ASV retention) and continues to invest in growth through acquisitions and R&D.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FactSet’s value proposition lies in its ability to deliver expansive, high-quality data and advanced analytics through an open, flexible, and AI-powered platform tailored to the complex workflows of investment professionals. The company emphasizes deep workflow integration, enterprise-wide solutions, and superior client service, differentiating itself through innovation, breadth of content, and the ability to automate and enhance decision-making across the investment lifecycle.
